bin: paste text, get a link. https://bin.rex.wf

Create
  cmd | curl --data-binary @- https://bin.rex.wf
  curl -T crash.log https://bin.rex.wf             the file name picks the highlighting
  curl -F a.ts=@a.ts -F b.ts=@b.ts https://bin.rex.wf   several files, one link
  Options go in the query string: title=...  lang=...  ttl=1h|1d|7d|30d|never (default never)
  The response is the link. Anonymous pastes also get a delete command.
  Send "Accept: application/json" (or add ?json) for a JSON receipt.

Read
  Browsers get a viewer. Everything else gets plain text, with terminal colours stripped.
  GET /<id>                          the paste
  GET /<id>?head=50  ?tail=50  ?lines=10-80   a slice (add &n=1 to number the lines)
  GET /<id>?grep=<text>&context=3    matching lines, like grep -n -C 3 (text, | for or, ^ $ anchors, .* wildcard)
  GET /<id>?digest                   a log's errors, warnings, summary and tail, with line numbers
  GET /<id>/<file>                   one file of a multi-file paste (GET /<id> lists them)
  GET /raw/<id>                      the exact bytes;  /dl/<id> downloads them
  GET /<a>/vs/<b>                    a unified diff of two pastes
  Response headers: x-bin-lines, x-bin-tokens (rough), x-bin-lang, x-bin-exit, x-bin-command.
  For big pastes (over ~10k tokens), read ?digest or a slice before the whole thing.

Delete
  curl -X DELETE https://bin.rex.wf/<id> -H 'x-delete: <token from the receipt>'

CLI (Node 20+): curl -fsSL https://bin.rex.wf/install | sh
  bin file.ts          bin a.ts b.ts          cmd | bin
  bin run -- bun test  runs the command, streams its output to a live paste, exits with its code
  bin get <id> [--digest | --grep <text> | --tail 50]

Limits: 2 MB per anonymous paste (10 files), 5 MB with the owner token, about 20 pastes a minute. Text only; nothing is ever rendered as HTML.
